statement: There is a constant U, depending only on the fixed residual data and Σ, with the following property. One can construct abelian, totally real 2-extensions Q ⊂ A ⊂ F in which 2 splits completely, together with allowed sets SA, SF , such that the following assertions hold. 1. The allowed sets contain the real and dyadic places and all places above Σ. Their numbers uA, uF of non-dyadic finite places are at most U. The degrees dA = [A : Q] and [F : A] can be made arbitrarily large, with d = [F : Q] = [F : A]dA. 2. If r̄ is absolutely irreducible, its restriction to GF is absolutely irreducible. In this case there are no marked places. 3. In the reducible case, the characters remain distinct on GF if they were distinct on GQ. If α2 ̸= 1, there are again no marked places. If α2 = 1, there is a dyadic place v0 of A and the marked set M consists of all its extensions to F. Set m = |M|; thus m = [F : A] and m/d = 1/dA in the marked case, whereas m = 0 otherwise. 4. In the reducible case, for β = α, α−1 the following group is zero: n c ∈ H1 (GF,SF , k(β)) : locv(c) = 0 for every v ∈ SF \ M o = 0. (25) Here the zero conditions include all real places. The condition at a marked place is unrestricted. 5. In the reducible case, restriction preserves residual extension classes: for either ratio β, the map H1 (GA,SA , k(β)) −→ H1 (GF,SF , k(β)) is injective. 43 In the reducible case let H1 str(F, k(β)) denote the Selmer group with zero condition at M, full condition at SF \ M (including the real places), and unramified condition elsewhere. Then dimk H1 str(F, k(β)) ≤ ( d + uF , α2 ̸= 1, 2d − 3m + uF , α2 = 1. (26)
